correctness.rationale: For every finite complete outward-directed q-ary tree, the bottom-up support and multiset descriptors exactly characterize ordinary and counting bisimulation. At q=2 support determines the size-two multiset. In general t_{k+1}=2*C(t_k+q-1,q) gives the universal O_q(N/log N) bound via height-level summation. For q>=3 the constrained coloring family has exactly h+2 ordinary classes and graded-root census g_1=q-1, g_{k+1}=C(g_k+q-1,q). The verified inequality g_2^(q-1)>q! supplies positive exponential-in-q^k type growth, allowing distinct types in Omega(N/log N) disjoint subtrees at residual height O(log h). The quotient-ratio upper and lower bounds therefore match Theta_q(N/(log N)^2); h+1 ordinary types force no graded splitting. The standalone verifier directly exercises 41,116 exhaustive finite colorings and 14 larger structural witnesses. No part of the infinite proof relies on extrapolating enumerations.

originality.rationale: The proposed contribution is the joint sharp arity threshold and maximal G/B asymptotic quotient ratio for the same binary coloring, attained with the smallest possible nontrivial ordinary quotient. This is not the standard fact that graded modalities distinguish multiplicity; inspected primary papers instead prove bisimulation invariance, expressive completeness and minimization algorithms. The ordinary-only complete-tree Theta(N/log N) bound does not cover graded quotients or a simultaneous separation with B=h+2. Targeted mathematical-result and primary-paper searches did not locate an equivalent theorem, but an unindexed general coalgebraic/tree minimization antecedent remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: The earlier tree-automata and coalgebraic literature is extensive; full priority exclusion cannot be guaranteed by semantic searching.
The precise same-tree extremal ratio might appear under an unindexed alternative vocabulary such as set-vs-bag state signatures, unordered-tree DAG compression, or rooted-tree multiset minimization.
The 2007 weighted tree-automaton paper was read only at metadata/abstract level and was not treated as decisive negative full-text evidence.

value.rationale: Ordinary and counting bisimulations are natural minimization equivalences, and the ratio of their quotient state counts on one input quantifies the cost of adding counting observations. The result determines the exact structural arity threshold and a sharp order-of-magnitude separation with only one propositional atom and an ordinary quotient of the minimum possible size that permits separation. It contributes a coherent extremal classification and explicit witness family, not a finite table or routine identity.
